correctness.summary: The fixed-variance maximum is reduced by Lagrange multipliers and strict convexity of Lambda'(x)-2 mu x to an isosceles angle triple. Lobachevsky duplication then gives a one-variable exact profile; monotonicity of a paired integral proves the sharp global quadratic constant, and a degenerating isosceles family proves optimality.

limitations: Only nondegenerate ideal tetrahedra in H^3 are covered.
The stability coordinate is Euclidean squared deviation of the three dihedral angles, not an intrinsic moduli-space metric.
No extension to finite, hyperideal, generalized, or higher-dimensional simplices is established.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; an equivalent special-function or folklore formulation may exist.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical maximal-volume simplex results, Thurston's qualitative near-maximality statement, angle-structure variational results, and later generalized-tetrahedron literature were checked. No located source states the exact fixed-dihedral-variance volume envelope, its equality family, or the sharp coefficient 3 v3/(2 pi^2).

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result converts classical uniqueness of the regular volume maximizer into an exact global stability profile and a best-constant inverse estimate for the dihedral angles.
